saints.name: St. Kateri Tekakwitha
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: The “Lily of the Mohawks,” a young Mohawk-Algonquin convert of New France whose purity and penance shone amid great opposition, and the first Native American…
biography: Kateri Tekakwitha — her name means 'she who bumps into things' — was born in 1656 at Ossernenon, a Mohawk village in what is now New York, daughter of a Mohawk chief and an Algonquin Christian captive. Smallpox killed her parents and brother when she was four, leaving her face scarred and her eyes dim.

Instructed by the Jesuit Jacques de Lamberville, she was baptized on Easter Sunday, 18 April 1676, taking the name Catherine after Catherine of Siena. Mocked and threatened for her faith and refusal of marriage, in 1677 she fled two hundred miles to the Christian mission of Kahnawake near Montreal.

There she nursed the sick and practiced penances her confessors had to restrain. At the Annunciation of 1679 she vowed perpetual virginity — the 'first Iroquois virgin.' She died on Holy Wednesday, 17 April 1680, aged twenty-four; within the quarter-hour her smallpox scars vanished, witnesses said.

Beatified by John Paul II in 1980 and canonized by Benedict XVI in 2012, the first Native American saint, the 'Lily of the Mohawks' is patroness of ecology, whose woods she hung with twig crosses; of exiles, having fled her village; and of orphans, as the smallpox left her.
saints.knownFor: Heroic purity, penance, and constancy under persecution among the Mohawk of New France.

canonization.canonized: 2012 by Pope Benedict XVI — the first Native American saint

sources.text: USCCB liturgical calendar — optional memorial, 14 July (USA); the general Roman calendar keeps her on 17 April
